question: True or false: telescopes can see galaxies that are receding from Earth faster than light?
answer: True. Relativity's speed limit governs motion through space, not the stretching of space. In the standard model, any galaxy whose light arrives stretched to over two and a half times its original wavelength is receding faster than light today. Many already were when that light set out; it was dragged backwards before it gained ground.
move: Check which rule a limit belongs to before applying it everywhere.
trap: Nothing moves faster than light, so no galaxy can recede faster.
